extracted.intended_audience: state policymakers, program planners, community-based organizations, and practitioners designing or funding fatherhood/parenting programs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for designing, operating, and funding community-based fatherhood programs (prevention, parenting education, employment linkage, incarceration reentry, and marriage/co-parenting supports). Targets programs serving young and low-income fathers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on responsibility in all life aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs focus on the need for young men to act responsibly in all aspects of their lives — not just when it comes to sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help boys understand that decisions made as teenagers affect schooling, relationships, and work; build a sense of control over their environments and long-term consequences of choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set high expectations for young men
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should set high expectations for young men and not 'baby' them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask whether participants are prepared to work and be responsible (e.g., prepared to work eight hours a day, five days a week); hold participants to meaningful standards rather than lowering expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate curriculum and emphasis for young men
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should have a separate curriculum and emphasis for young men since strategies that work for girls may not resonate with boys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design content reflecting male role models and cultural references; use competitive or goal-oriented approaches when appropriate; avoid simply adapting girl-focused curricula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give boys hope for the future
rubrics_metrics.description: Good pregnancy prevention and fatherhood programs give young men hope and alternatives for proving manhood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address fatalism (e.g., 'I don't expect to see my 25th birthday') by presenting future-oriented opportunities, education and employment pathways, and legacy-building alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide close connection to an adult role model (preferably a man)
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful programs provide boys a close connection to an adult role model — preferably a man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruit mentors, veteran fathers, or male staff; recognize high father absence in low-income communities and prioritize male role modeling to teach gender roles and parenting behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach practical life and parenting skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should prepare young men to assume practical responsibilities of fatherhood (e.g., life skills, home economics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include instruction in balancing a checkbook, diaper changing, age-appropriate play, and other day-to-day parenting skills; such skills both prepare men and may discourage premature parenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive parenting curriculum covering parenting, health, legal, employment, and money management
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a comprehensive curriculum that spans pregnancy and birth, child development and health, legal issues (child support, custody), employment, education, and money management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train site coordinators to implement multi-book curricula (example: MELD’s 10-book, 27-topic curriculum); adapt materials for target populations (Hmong, Latino, deaf, special-needs parents, teen mothers, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Train site coordinators and community volunteer leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should train site coordinators, who then train community volunteers to lead groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build local capacity by certifying coordinators and volunteers; provide ongoing staff development and supervision to maintain fidelity to curriculum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruit through community touchpoints and offer participation incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruit participants in hospitals, schools, sports leagues, and other places frequented by young fathers; provide incentives like free food, transportation, and child care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both voluntary recruitment and accept mandated referrals (courts, probation) when appropriate; remove logistical barriers to attendance to maximize participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer mentoring and hands-on skills training
rubrics_metrics.description: Pair first-time fathers with 'veteran fathers' to learn hands-on caregiving skills (holding, feeding, changing, bathing) and child development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create cycles where new fathers become veteran mentors after a few months to sustain peer networks (example: Boot Camp for New Dads model).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include employment, education, and money-management components
rubrics_metrics.description: Parenting programs should include practical advice and services related to employment, education, and money management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate job-readiness training, resume help, education counseling, and financial literacy to address economic barriers to responsible fatherhood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate parenting education into school curricula
rubrics_metrics.description: State education agencies should revise abstinence/sex education curricula to include components on fathering and require young men to study child health and development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed fathering responsibilities and child development modules in middle and high school classes to reach boys before they become parents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide funding and technical assistance to community and faith-based fatherhood programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Governors and legislators should offer technical assistance and financial support to community-based organizations and faith communities organizing fatherhood education and support groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer start-up funding, training, and ongoing technical help to expand effective locally based models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link father involvement programs to services for new mothers
rubrics_metrics.description: Fund father involvement programs that are linked to programs serving new mothers (e.g., WIC, Healthy Start).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate outreach and service delivery to both parents through maternal-child health platforms to normalize father participation and reduce stigma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connect paternity establishment to parenting supports
rubrics_metrics.description: Child support enforcement offices should link paternity-establishment programs to support programs for new fathers, and fathers who establish paternity should have access to parenting education and support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use paternity events and child-support touchpoints to offer parenting classes, case management, and referrals rather than only enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support programs for incarcerated fathers and reentry
rubrics_metrics.description: Support programs that work with incarcerated fathers to help them stay connected to children while in prison and become better parents after release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide in-prison peer-led groups, train inmate facilitators, offer parenting, communication, anger management, and reentry planning, and coordinate with community services on release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make programming culturally relevant and address racism
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailor curricula to reflect participants' cultural experiences and address issues such as racism and heritage pride where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design modules that give tools to cope with racism and foster cultural pride; adapt messaging and examples to participant communities (as CFWD does for African-American men).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize team parenting, communication, and decision-making skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should emphasize team parenting, respectful relationships, improved decision-making, and better communication even when parents are not married.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach joint decision-making, conflict resolution, and communication strategies focused on children's best interests ('child-centered' approach).

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-parenting curriculum and mediation services
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide co-parenting curricula that teach fathers (and mothers) positive communication, include mothers in group supports, and offer mediation sessions to negotiate visitation and custody issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multi-session support groups for custodial parents, invite both parents to mediation, and provide follow-up mediation services for up to six months or as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address domestic violence and screen for safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Fatherhood programs receiving state funds should train staff to spot domestic violence, report suspected abuse, provide referrals, and assess when a non-custodial parent presents a potential danger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer domestic-violence-specific support groups/seminars, individual counseling, and coordinate with shelters and victim services; when appropriate, work with both parents toward non-violent parenting arrangements while prioritizing safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote healthy marriage skills where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: When promoting marriage, emphasize healthy marriage skills (negotiation, anger management, budgeting) and provide marriage education rather than simply advocating marriage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support modeling approaches (couples living in communities as examples), pre-marital counseling, marriage preparation classes, mentoring, and retreats; ensure inclusiveness and avoid stigmatizing single-parent families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require access to comprehensive employment services
rubrics_metrics.description: Employment programs for fathers must be comprehensive and include one-on-one case management and counseling; résumé and interview preparation; job-search assistance; access to short-term and longer training programs; on-the-job training and paid work experience; referrals to medical, mental health, and substance-abuse treatment; access to professional clothing; transportation assistance; and job-retention services (including mediation between workers and employers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate employment services into fatherhood programs or require partnerships so that employment barriers are addressed alongside parenting education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide legal assistance to remove employment barriers
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should help fathers resolve legal barriers to employment (criminal records, suspended licenses, unpaid fines) through legal staff or partnerships with legal services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services can include negotiating fines/penalties, sealing/expunging records, contesting paternity, negotiating child-support modifications, fighting evictions, and facilitating bankruptcy when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate workforce, welfare, and parenting services
rubrics_metrics.description: State workforce development and welfare agencies should require employment programs receiving state funds to partner with or provide referrals to parenting programs, and parenting programs to link with employment and training programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require formal linkages and referral pathways to create integrated service delivery; use funding rules to incentivize partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require court and child-support referrals to employment programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts should refer men with child-support arrearages to employment programs, and child-support enforcement offices should coordinate with responsible fatherhood programs and pursue modification orders for low-income fathers making good-faith job efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use referrals as an alternative to incarceration and use modification mechanisms to adjust orders during job search or training periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use TANF and public funds to support integrated services and legal partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Governors and legislators should use TANF and other funds to provide grants that enable employment and training programs to hire lawyers or develop partnerships with legal services offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund legal assistance and service integration to remove barriers to employment and family involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connect participants directly to employers and employer networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should develop relationships with local employers and job-training agencies, keep updated vacancy and eligibility information, and refer fathers directly to jobs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain employer lists, referral specialists, and active placement strategies to increase placement and retention (example: Fathers That Work maintains relationships with 29 area employers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide flexible support orders for young fathers in school
rubrics_metrics.description: For fathers under age 25, offer flexible child-support orders so they can remain in school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with courts to design support orders that allow continued education while meeting child-support obligations as income changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use father advocates and intensive case management
rubrics_metrics.description: Deploy 'father advocates' who provide one-on-one intensive case management, practical assistance (rides, references), and ongoing support tailored to fathers’ needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates should help with job search, legal navigation, referrals, and linkages to other services; these personalized supports increase employment retention and parenting involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer low-cost or waived legal clinics and seminars
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide legal seminars and low-fee (or waived in hardship cases) legal advice on paternity establishment, child support, and related issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold regular clinics, partner with legal services, and use modest fees with hardship waivers to broaden access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design programs to reduce stigma (open-to-public options)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer classes and services in open-to-the-public settings so program participants do not feel stigmatized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locate classes at community colleges or public venues and integrate services with other public offerings to normalize participation (example: Santa Barbara 12-hour parenting class open to public).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor, evaluate and adapt programs (use independent evaluations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should be subject to independent evaluation to assess outcomes (e.g., employment, child-support payments, domestic-violence reduction) and adapt models accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect data on participant employment, retention, paternity establishment, parenting involvement, and domestic violence incidence; use evaluations (such as university-led studies) to refine program design.
